prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 227: the joint transit and radial-velocity likelihood with the star's uncertainty inside (tranche T3 by D-R10-207-01)
committed: before any of the joint model existed in js/inference: the shared-phase model, the planet's mass, radius and density, the stellar inputs and their propagation, the validator, the oracle's results, the ensembles, any panel, diagram or lesson step. The systems, seeds, cadences and noise below are written out so that the oracle (numpy, scipy and batman: no Gravitas code) builds its own data and the harness builds the same kind of systems. Nothing was tuned against code that did not exist.
rule: A crossed bound is a failed check, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured, or whose data was never supplied, is NOT RUN and says why. An amendment is recorded with its reason and never changes a bound already judged.

supply.note: Two public items are fetched only by the coordinator and none exists at commit time. (1) A public radial-velocity series for a transiting planet, with its citation and a rights row, for leg E1 (a published joint solution reproduced under a fixed contract). (2) A published table of mass-radius composition curves (Zeng et al. 2019) for the diagram. Without (1) the leg E1 is NOT RUN; without (2) the diagram draws the constant-density lines (analytic) and the bulk density classes of Prompt 203, and says that no composition curve is shipped. Nothing is typed from memory, and no table ships in the application unless it was supplied.

constants.note: CODATA 2018 G; IAU 2015 B3 nominal GM of the Sun, Jupiter and the Earth and the nominal solar and equatorial radii of the Sun, Jupiter and the Earth. Masses in solar or Jupiter units are ratios of the nominal GMs, so G cancels in the planet's mass from the amplitude; G enters only the densities.

scope.built: one joint likelihood over a transit light curve and radial velocities that share the period and the epoch of inferior conjunction, and the eccentricity of the radial-velocity orbit (the transit is the circular-orbit model with the first-order eccentric scaling of the duration, a stated approximation); the planet's mass (the amplitude, the stated stellar mass, the inclination the transit fixes), radius (the radius ratio times the stated stellar radius) and bulk density with the covariance of the whole fit and the stellar mass and radius, with their uncertainty and their correlation, carried through; the star's density from the transit against the star's density from its stated mass and radius as a consistency check; and the refusals: no planetary mass, radius or density without the stellar term it needs, a minimum mass only from velocities alone, a jitter at its bound flagged.
scope.notBuilt: a second planet, a trend, a Gaussian-process noise model, rotational distortion, the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect, the planet's atmosphere; the stellar parameters are inputs with a stated uncertainty and are never fitted here (a stellar fit is Prompt 219's isochrone fit, named as a provenance, not run).

systems.note: Truth for every synthetic leg. The planet is built from its mass, so the oracle derives the amplitude from the mass by an independent route (a three-dimensional orbit, the line-of-sight velocity by differentiating the position), and the harness derives it from the formula under test. a is from Kepler's third law with the sum of the masses; a/R* is a over the stellar radius; the inclination is acos of the conjunction impact parameter times (1 + e sin w) over (a/R* (1 - e^2)).

S1.what: a hot Jupiter on a circular orbit

S3.what: a Neptune-mass planet: a small amplitude against the same errors

S4.what: S1's star and orbit with a grazing geometry (b + k > 1)

stellar.note: The stated stellar inputs of every leg, a catalog-like entry: the analyst is given these, never the truth. Mass and radius are positively correlated, as an isochrone fit leaves them.

rv.timesDrawn: uniform over the span, numpy default_rng(227), sorted; the first 15 are instrument 0

sampling.ensembleRv: 30 epochs uniform over 40 days (seeded), two instruments of 15, zero points 12 and -25 m/s, stated error 3.0 m/s, true jitter 2.0 m/s

fit.note: Every fit leaves the zero points per instrument linear, the baseline linear and the jitter searched, as the core does.

coverage.truthStar: for each replicate the TRUE star is drawn from the stated mass and radius with the stated sigmas and correlation (a catalog value is a draw from its own error distribution); the data are made for that true star and the true planet mass, radius ratio and geometry; the analyst is handed the stated (central) mass, radius and sigmas and never the draw
coverage.target: the one-sigma interval (the fit's value plus and minus its propagated sigma, the 68.3 percent normal interval) holds each replicate's own true Mp, Rp and rho_p at a rate in the stated bound

ensembles.falsePositiveFlag: the stellar-density tension flag, over the same replicates

definitions.massFromK: Mp sin i is the root of K = (2 pi G / P)^(1/3) Mp sin i / ((Ms + Mp)^(2/3) sqrt(1 - e^2)) in Mp (the sum of the masses, not the small-mass approximation); the mass is Mp sin i / sin i with sin i from the transit. Without a transit the result is Mp sin i, named the minimum mass.
definitions.radius: Rp = k Rs, in Jupiter radii (equatorial, 71492 km) with Rs in solar radii of 695700 km.
definitions.density: rho_p = Mp / (4 pi Rp^3 / 3), in g/cm^3; reported only when Mp, Rs and Ms each have a stated uncertainty; the linearized sigma carries the fit's covariance (the rows of the whole fit's covariance for K, e cos w, e sin w, P, k, a/R*, b) and the star's two sigmas with their correlation; the Monte Carlo propagation of the statistics kernel (Prompt 154) draws the fit's parameters and the star jointly and its intervals are the percentile intervals.
definitions.starDensity: rho_star,transit = 3 pi (a/R*)^3 / (G P^2) with a/R* the eccentric-corrected true value; rho_star,stated = Ms / (4 pi Rs^3 / 3). The tension is z = (rho_star,transit - rho_star,stated) / sqrt(sigma_t^2 + sigma_s^2) with the first-order sigma of each, flagged when |z| exceeds 3.
definitions.eccentricTransit: the transit uses the circular-orbit model with a/R*(circ) = a/R*(true) (1 + e sin w) / sqrt(1 - e^2) and the conjunction impact parameter b = a/R* cos i (1 - e^2)/(1 + e sin w), the first-order duration scaling (Winn 2010); w is the planet's argument of periastron, the same w as rv.js and as batman's w, which A5 checks against a three-dimensional orbit.
definitions.stellarShare: the fraction of the variance of a derived planetary quantity that the star's two inputs carry: 1 - (sigma of the fit alone / total sigma)^2, from the same linearization

checks.what: the planet's mass from K, P, e, sin i and the stellar mass equals the oracle's root find of the full relation (scipy brentq, astropy constants for the ratios), relative, over 12 cases from 0.1 to 8 Jupiter masses and e up to 0.6
Jupiter around the Sun (P 4332.589 d, e 0 and i 90) produces K between the stated bounds, and the inversion returns one Jupiter mass: an anchor to the published 12.4 m/s
the Earth around the Sun (P 365.25636 d) produces K between the stated bounds (the published 9 cm/s)
the bulk density of a planet of one Jupiter mass and one equatorial Jupiter radius equals the oracle's value from the nominal GM and G, relative

rv.js's velocity curve (the same w as batman) equals the line-of-sight velocity of the star in a three-dimensional two-body orbit differentiated numerically (the oracle), over e in 0, 0.2, 0.5 and w in 0, 40, 120, 250 degrees, as a fraction of K, and the star is receding after the transit when the planet is in front

the total transit duration of the eccentric-orbit mapping (the circular-equivalent a/R*) against batman's exact eccentric light curve, relative, for e 0.1 and 0.2 at w 40, 90 and 250 degrees (the stated first-order approximation)

the joint model with an infinite stellar-mass and radius uncertainty removed (sigma 0) returns the same derived planet quantities as the closed formulas for the fit's own values, and its linearized sigma equals the quadrature of the fit-only sigma and the star's, for uncorrelated inputs, relative
the statistics kernel's propagation of the planet's mass, radius and density (20,000 draws, a fixed seed) against the linearized sigma, relative, on S1's fit
rvMonteCarlo.js's percentile and the kernel's percentile interval agree on one fixed array (the duplication removed where identical)

S1 (the oracle's own data: batman light curve, 30 velocities, two instruments, numpy noise): the joint fit's t0, P, k, a/R*, b, K, e cos w, e sin w against the oracle's joint least-squares solution (batman, scipy, the same quadratic law in q1, q2, the jitter by the same -2 ln L search), in the oracle's sigma

S1: the derived Mp, Rp and rho_p (with the stated star) against the oracle's, relative, and their sigma against the oracle's Monte Carlo of 400,000 draws from its covariance and the stated star, relative
S2 (eccentric): the same comparison, with the oracle using batman's exact eccentric orbit and the joint model its first-order mapping; the amplitude, e cos w, e sin w and P, t0 in the oracle's sigma
S2: derived Mp, Rp and rho_p against the oracle's, relative
S1: the jitter the joint fit finds against the oracle's, absolute, in m/s

S1 recovered from the harness's own forward model (one seeded realization): t0, P, k, a/R*, b, K within 4 of their own sigma of the truth; the derived Mp, Rp, rho_p within 4 of their propagated sigma of the truth of THAT realization's star
S3 (Neptune mass): K and the planet's mass within 4 sigma of the truth, and the mass is reported with a sigma at least 20 percent of its value (a small signal is not given a small error bar)
S2 recovered (the eccentric orbit): e cos w and e sin w within 4 sigma and the derived mass within 4 sigma of the truth
the one-sigma interval of the planet's mass, with the star's mass inside it, holds each replicate's true mass
the same for the planet's radius
the same for the planet's bulk density

CONTROL: the planet's radius and density intervals from the fit alone, the star's uncertainty left out, hold the truth at a rate BELOW the bound (the review's correction: the planet's density is only as good as the star's); the omission must be visible
the amplitude K's own one-sigma interval holds the truth
the stellar-density tension flag is raised on at most this fraction of the replicates, whose star is consistent by construction
S1's velocities with no transit: the result is the minimum mass Mp sin i, labelled as such, with the mass function; no planet radius, no density, no inclination, and no value named Mp
velocities with a true jitter of 40 m/s against a jitter bound of 20 m/s: the fit says the jitter is at its bound (a warning and a flag on the result), and no mass is reported without the flag
S1 with no stellar mass: no mass and no density, only the amplitude and the mass function; with a radius and no mass: the radius and no density; with neither: no planet radius in Jupiter units

a stellar mass and radius stated without their uncertainty: the planet's mass, radius and density are REFUSED with the named reason (the stellar uncertainty is required), never reported with the star taken as exact
S1 with a stated star whose density is 5 sigma from the transit's: the tension is flagged (|z| > 3) and the result says the planet's density is as good as that star
S4 (grazing): the inclination, hence the planet's mass and density, is not constrained and the result says so

S1's velocities with an unmodelled second planet (amplitude 20 m/s, period 11.6 d): the fit's jitter is larger than the stated error of the velocities and the result says the velocities are not described by one planet

a published joint transit and radial-velocity solution reproduced within its stated uncertainties under a fixed contract (the contract is written when the data arrive and before any fit); NOT RUN until the public velocity series is supplied
